instruction.name: xvldrepl.b
instruction.description: Read 8-bit data from memory address `addr + offset`, replicate the data to all vector lanes and save into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. The `offset` operand is a byte offset, matching the assembly immediate; the encoded instruction stores it as a scaled immediate for wider elements.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvldrepl.b $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.b $xr1, $r20, 1; xvldrepl.b $xr2, $r20, 2; xvldrepl.b $xr3, $r20, 3; xvldrepl.b $xr4, $r20, 4; xvldrepl.b $xr5, $r20, 5; xvldrepl.b $xr6, $r20, 6; xvldrepl.b $xr7, $r20, 7
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024' --asm 'xvldrepl.b $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.b $xr1, $r20, 1; xvldrepl.b $xr2, $r20, 2; xvldrepl.b $xr3, $r20, 3; xvldrepl.b $xr4, $r20, 4; xvldrepl.b $xr5, $r20, 5; xvldrepl.b $xr6, $r20, 6; xvldrepl.b $xr7, $r20, 7'

notes: Vector memory operation. Throughput measured with a hot 1KB stack buffer; latency not measured because it depends on cache/coherence state and needs a separate dependency chain.
